subject: Using Stan to compute posterior in parameter estimation problem

messages.author: a9f4f64c95831835
messages.subject: Using Stan to compute posterior in parameter estimation problem
parts:
I m wondering if Stan could be used to estimate the posterior density of the parameters conditioned on the measurements in general nonlinear parameter estimation problems. Say that

y = f(x; \theta) + w

where y are the measurents, x are (deterministic) control variables and \theta are the model parameters to be estimated. f() is a nonlinear deterministic function and w are measurement errors drawn from a known distribution. The parameters of this distribution are generally known, however it would useful to infer them as well of course. What would be interesting is to explore the shape of the posterior p( \theta | y,x ) for different "measurement configurations".

-Arrigo

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Using Stan to compute posterior in parameter estimation problem
parts:
Hi Arrigo,

Yes. That's pretty much what Stan's built for. You have to specify y, theta, x, f(), and the measurement distribution and you've got a Stan program.


Daniel
